newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour pledges VAT on fuel as first tax cut.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour pledges VAT on fuel as first tax cut.

text.p: The first tax cut by a UK Labour government would be reduce value-added-tax (VAT) on fuel to five percent, the British opposition party said in a policy document.
The document, entitled "Leading Britain into the Future", also said Labour would set a rigorous inflation target. But it did not elaborate.
VAT on heating fuel is currently levied at eight percent.
"The first tax cut should be to reduce VAT on fuel to five percent -- the lowest it can be -- which will help pensioners in particular," the document said.
The document, released ahead of a news conference by opposition leader Tony Blair, said Labour would be the party of sound finance.
